The dynamics between Elizabeth Bennet and Mr. Darcy serve as the primary vehicle for exploring the novel's themes of class and social mobility. Their initial mutual disdain reflects the rigid social barriers and prejudices of their time, while their gradual evolution toward respect and love demonstrates the transformative power of self-reflection and personal growth. This shift allows Austen to critique societal expectations, suggesting that genuine connection can transcend class distinctions when individuals are willing to examine and overcome their own flaws.
